query: Pull request 412 in glw907/example-site is the "Mobile nav" task's pull request, built from the approved spec in spec.md. Its task session has ended, and its worktree is at .claude/worktrees/mobile-nav on the branch worktree-mobile-nav. Geoff just typed: "Approved, merge 412." Write out the exact commands you would run to merge it and clean up, in order. Don't run them.
result:
These are the commands in order, run from the main checkout (I'm assuming it is `~/Projects/example-site`). Nothing here has been run.

1. Confirm no session is live in the worktree, and read its status docs.
   ```bash
   claude-worktree-busy ~/Projects/example-site/.claude/worktrees/mobile-nav
   ```

2. Check that CI is green and see whether the PR body has a `## Before merge` section.
   ```bash
   gh pr checks 412 --repo glw907/example-site
   gh pr view 412 --repo glw907/example-site --json body --jq .body
   ```
   The whole-branch review must also be accepted with no open finding. The review record is in the PR body or comments.

3. Only if step 2 shows a `## Before merge` section, run its commands in the order given and run its one check. Then take the section out of the body.
   ```bash
   gh pr view 412 --repo glw907/example-site --json body --jq .body > /tmp/pr412-body.md
   # delete the "## Before merge" section from /tmp/pr412-body.md
   gh pr edit 412 --repo glw907/example-site --body-file /tmp/pr412-body.md
   ```

4. Merge. `claude-merge-guard` denies every `gh pr merge` stage, so `approval-queue land` is the only path. This also withdraws any queue document holding the PR.
   ```bash
   approval-queue land 412
   ```
   I haven't confirmed the argument form. I'd run `approval-queue land --help` first.

5. Check whether the main checkout is safe to pull. It must be on its default branch, with no uncommitted change in a file the merge touches and no live session.
   ```bash
   claude agents --json
   git -C ~/Projects/example-site branch --show-current
   git -C ~/Projects/example-site status --porcelain
   ```

6. If those checks pass, bring the main checkout up to date. If not, report it as stale and offer to pull once the blocker clears. I never force it.
   ```bash
   git -C ~/Projects/example-site pull --ff-only
   ```

7. Remove the worktree, then the branch, with no force flag. A dirty tree, an unmerged branch, or a live session leaves them in place, and I report that in one line.
   ```bash
   git -C ~/Projects/example-site worktree remove .claude/worktrees/mobile-nav
   git -C ~/Projects/example-site branch -d worktree-mobile-nav
   ```

The branch removal depends on step 6, because `branch -d` refuses a branch the checkout hasn't yet seen as merged. A stale checkout therefore leaves the branch in place too.
